For prophylaxis, the recommended dose is 1500 mg per day, taken orally either as a single daily dose or divided into two doses (BID), and always with food. Alternatively, administer 1000 mg of the medication combined with 400 mg of proguanil orally once daily for 3 days. Dosing for Patients Aged <13 Years: The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established for patients under 13 years of age. Dosing for Patients Aged >13 Years: Administer 1500 mg (equivalent to 10 mL) once daily with food. Alternatively, administer 750 mg (equivalent to 5 mL) twice daily (total daily dose: 1500 mg) with food for 21 days. Weight-Based Dosing (with Proguanil): For patients weighing 11–20 kg: Administer 250 mg of the medication with 100 mg of proguanil once daily for 3 days. For patients weighing 21–30 kg: Administer 500 mg of the medication with 200 mg of proguanil once daily for 3 days. For patients weighing 31–40 kg: Administer 750 mg of the medication with 300 mg of proguanil once daily for 3 days. Drug Interactions: 1. Atovaquone and Dapsone (Topical): Avoid co-administration of topical dapsone with oral dapsone or antimalarial medications due to the risk of hemolytic reactions. Use alternative drugs if necessary. 2. Atovaquone and Efavirenz: Efavirenz reduces atovaquone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 3. Atovaquone and Indinavir: Indinavir decreases atovaquone levels through an unknown mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 4. Atovaquone and Metoclopramide (Intranasal): Metoclopramide may increase atovaquone levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor. However, metoclopramide may also reduce atovaquone absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 5. Atovaquone and Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases atovaquone levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Atovaquone and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases atovaquone levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Atovaquone and Tetracycline: Tetracycline reduces atovaquone levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor but should still be monitored. 8. Atovaquone and Warfarin: Atovaquone increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Pharmacokinetics and Administration: Oral absorption of atovaquone is limited but significantly enhanced when taken with food. Failure to administer with food may result in lower plasma concentrations and reduced therapeutic efficacy. The medication undergoes enterohepatic recirculation, with a bioavailability of 23% for tablets and 47% for the suspension form. The elimination half-life is approximately 2–3 days, and the drug is primarily excreted unchanged in feces (94%). Warnings and Precautions: Hepatic Impairment: Cases of cholestatic hepatitis, elevated liver enzymes, and fatal liver failure have been reported. Patients with severe hepatic impairment should be closely monitored. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Rare but serious allergic reactions, including bronchospasm, angioedema, urticaria, and throat tightness, have been reported. Discontinue use if hypersensitivity occurs. Pregnancy and Lactation: Atovaquone is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk; use with caution in lactating patients. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, insomnia, and nasal congestion. A mild rash may occur, which is usually not serious. However, it is important to differentiate this from a rare rash indicative of a severe reaction. Serious allergic reactions are rare but require immediate medical attention. Storage Instructions: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom or freeze the product, as freezing reduces the drug's bioavailability and efficacy. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into drains unless instructed to do so. Overdose Management: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. For non-emergencies, contact a poison control center (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S.). Important Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your healthcare provider. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
